newsitem.title: USA: GTE offers 14 cent flat rate long distance.
newsitem.headline: GTE offers 14 cent flat rate long distance.

text.p: GTE Corp on Wednesday said it was offering a nationwide flat rate long distance calling plan for residential customers of $0.14 per minute, one cent below AT&T Corp's flat rate launched last year.
The plan has no monthly or enrollment fee and is available to consumers in 27 states where GTE offers other services.

GTE entered the long distance business in March 1996 and has amassed 800,000 customers. Analysts say that it and other new entrants have made a noticeable impact on AT&T in its core residential customer base.
"This plan truly takes the guesswork out of long distance calling," said Rob McCoy, president of GTE long distance.
He predicted that customers who seek simplicity, and those who make most of their calls during the day would be most attracted by the plan, called "GTE's One Easy Rate".
GTE last month unveiled a flat-rate calling plan for businesses, which included domestic and international calling.

GTE Corp is often compared with regional Bells, but unlike them it is not restricted by the 1996 Telecommunications Act which forces Bells to open their local calling regions to competition before offering long distance to local customers.
GTE's local calling regions are spread across the country in small areas, so it was never ruled a dominant carrier in any region.
Analysts say this ruling has been a boon for GTE, giving it a headstart of more than a year over the Bells in the $80 billion long distance market.
